source: CAMIL GE-V-06 · Page 11 · Meals and Food (ingredients half)
notes: The ingredient half of page 11: the categories food is bought and cooked in, as against
the Meals and Drinks area, which is what ends up on a plate at a given hour.
'salt' and 'sugar' are placed where they are used rather than in a bucket unit of their
own — salt with the salad, sugar with the dessert.
'watermelon' and 'grapes' moved out of the page's dessert row into the fruit unit, which
Two normalisations: MEAT BALLS -> meatballs, one word in standard English, and SHRIMPS ->
shrimp, which is how Americans use it.
'chop' is pinned to the cut of meat, not the verb.
'orange' is here as the fruit and also appears inside 'orange juice' in Meals and Drinks,
and as a colour in Colors. Three different areas, so no exercise can put them together.
VERY_EASY: an A1/A2 course, still its early pages.

area.name: Food and Ingredients
area.description: Los alimentos por familias: las verduras y la ensalada, las carnes, el pescado y los mariscos, la fruta y los postres.

units.name: Salad and vegetables
units.topic: What goes into a salad and the vegetables you buy at a market, and the one thing you season them with

units.name: Meat
units.topic: The meats and the ways they are served. 'chop' here is a cut of meat with the bone in, never the verb for cutting

units.name: Fish and seafood
units.topic: What comes out of the sea. 'fish' is the animal you eat, 'seafood' is everything edible from the sea, and 'shellfish' is the part of it that has a shell — the unit should keep those apart

units.name: Fruit
units.topic: The fruits a learner meets first, from the everyday ones to the large sweet ones

units.name: Dessert
units.topic: What is served at the end of a meal, and what makes it sweet
